purpose: Convert PursuitDesk access profiles, route skeleton, and database migration boundaries into backend session, tenant, section, commercial vault, membership admin, mutation, safe error, and denied-audit guardrails.

sourceAccessModel.rule: Company admins can see Membership Model; editors and viewers cannot be granted membership access.

guardFiles.policy: Verify signed session, expiry, inactive user, password reset freshness, and actor context.
Hash passwords, expire reset links, block reused reset tokens, and avoid secret logging.
Attach request id, actor id, company id, route id, and safe logger scope.
Resolve company scope from session only and reject payload, query, or route tenant spoofing.
Check section key, can_view, can_edit, admin-only rooms, and inactive user state.
Protect value, agreement, LOA, negotiation, forecast, billing, and management export facts.
Allow membership, plan, invoice, seat, subscription, and user-invite changes only for company admins.
Append denied access, tenant mismatch, commercial denial, admin denial, and edit denial events.
Centralize section keys, route groups, edit modes, commercial modes, and system-action exceptions.
Run every role and route against tenant, section, edit, vault, membership, and audit expectations.

middlewareOrder.rule: Create request id, logger scope, response timing, and blank actor shell before auth.
Throttle login, password reset, import commit, export, and billing webhook abuse paths.
Verify signed session, account status, expiry, and fresh-session requirement for sensitive routes.
Resolve company_id from the server-side session and block cross-company identifiers.
Match route group to section grant and decide view/edit permission before controller logic.
Block restricted value, agreement, negotiation, forecast, and report fields unless granted.
Require can_edit, optimistic version, and safe field list for create/update/delete paths.
Require company admin for users, seats, plan, invoice, subscription, and access template changes.
Write allowed and denied events with actor, tenant, target, route, request id, and result.
Return validation, auth, access, tenant, commercial, conflict, and server errors without leaking data.

tenantIsolationRules.detail: company_id comes from the verified session, never from browser payload.
Tenant-owned tables require company_id and foreign keys back to company-owned records.
record_id, client_id, import_batch_id, invoice_id, and report_id are verified before service calls.
Search, filters, quick jump, CSV export, report export, and client memory stay tenant-filtered.
Evidence files and source workbooks use company-scoped storage paths and signed URLs.
Dry-run, commit, rollback, and quarantine decisions can only touch the active company batch.
Webhook events map to one subscription and one company before changing access state.
Allowed and denied events carry company_id even when the user is denied.

deniedAuditEvents.detail: Email/password failed or inactive user tried to sign in.
Request tried to read or mutate another company record, batch, invoice, or export.
User tried to open a section without can_view access.
User tried to create, update, delete, import, dispatch, or export without can_edit access.
User tried to read value, agreement, LOA, negotiation, forecast, or restricted report data.
Non-admin tried to change seats, plan, invoices, users, or access templates.
User tried to commit or roll back an import batch without import/governance access.
User tried to read governance audit events without governance/admin access.

guardTests.expectation: POST /auth/login denies inactive user and writes auth.login.failed.
GET /records/:id with another company record never leaks existence.

guardTests.test: Operations user cannot see commercial facts
guardTests.expectation: GET /commercial/records/:id returns denied audit for tracker-only user.
PATCH /records/:id denies can_edit and writes section.edit.denied.
GET /commercial/dashboard succeeds for user with insight grant.

guardTests.test: Import owner can dry-run only inside tenant
guardTests.expectation: POST /imports/dry-run accepts same-company batch and blocks foreign batch ids.
Webhook validates signature and maps external subscription to exactly one company.
DELETE /audit/:id is unavailable and audit export remains admin/governance scoped.
GET /records/export never includes value, agreement, invoice, LOA, or negotiation fields.

sessionPolicy.detail: Hash with strong adaptive hashing; never log passwords or reset tokens.
One-time, short-lived, company-scoped, and invalidated after use.
Idle timeout plus absolute timeout; admin sensitive routes require fresh session.
Company admin invites user; invite accepts only the invited email and company.
Inactive users cannot sign in, cannot refresh sessions, and keep historical audit identity.
Make admin MFA a production gate before larger customers.
Billing webhooks, scheduled jobs, and import workers use system actor with tenant target.
Auth and access errors reveal no company, user, record, invoice, or commercial fact details.

routeGuardMap.guard: No tenant before login; tenant after session refresh
routeGuardMap.checks: Login rate limit, inactive user, reset token, session audit
Admin role, section grant updates, invite audit, preview state
Tenders/Projects grants, edit mode, redacted export, record ownership
Insight grant, commercial facts, forecast, agreements, negotiations
Dry-run, commit, rollback, source trace, quarantine ownership
Plan, seats, invoice, subscription, webhook mapping
Feedback session, item owner, sponsor export, retest state
Audit filters, exports, denial events, retention evidence
Management pack, redaction profile, commercial export gate

nonNegotiableRules: company_id comes from the verified server-side session.
Never trust tenant ids, company ids, or user ids from browser payloads.
Tenders and Projects routes return operational tracker fields only.
Commercial vault facts require explicit commercial or management access.
Membership Model requires company admin role.
Every denied sensitive action writes an audit event.
CSV exports and reports use a redaction profile.
Inactive users cannot sign in or refresh a session.
Webhook and scheduled jobs use system actor context with a single tenant target.
Safe errors never reveal hidden company, record, invoice, user, or commercial fact existence.
